en.name: Rosemary, fresh
en.summary: Fresh rosemary keeps 1–2 weeks at room temperature with the stems in water, and 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Its needles are stiff, waxy and resinous, which is why it outlasts every soft herb in the drawer.
en.pantry: 1–2 weeks standing in a jar with a little water, out of direct sun, with the water changed daily. Rosemary is a Mediterranean shrub and dry air suits it; what happens on the counter is that the sprigs slowly dry rather than rot, and dried rosemary is a perfectly good ingredient. Woody stems left in water too long will slime at the cut ends, so trim them when you change the water.
en.fridge: 2–3 weeks at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, wrapped loosely in dry kitchen paper inside a bag or box in the crisper. Do not wash it until you cook — the needles shed water badly, and any that gets trapped against the stem stays there. Keep the bag away from the back wall, where the needles can freeze and blacken. If the paper feels damp after a few days, swap it for a dry sheet.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given, because freeze damage will appear: the needles darken and go soft, and a thawed sprig cannot be stripped cleanly. The flavour itself survives freezing well, since it sits in resinous oils rather than fragile volatiles, so frozen sprigs are still fine dropped straight into a braise or a roasting tin. For anything where the herb is seen or chewed, dry the surplus instead — hang a bunch upside down somewhere airy and strip the needles into a jar.
en.thawing: Do not thaw. Put frozen sprigs straight into the pan, the pot or the roasting tin.
spoilage: Needles gone black or dark brown rather than grey-green.
Slime at the cut end of a woody stem that has sat in water.
White or grey fuzz on the stem inside a closed bag.
No resinous smell at all when a needle is crushed.
tips: Strip the needles downwards, against the direction they grow; upwards they shred.
Keep the bare stems — they make good skewers for grilling.
Dry the surplus rather than freezing it; rosemary dries better than almost any herb.
Add it early in cooking, not at the end: the resinous oils need heat and time.

faq.q: How long does fresh rosemary last?
faq.a: 1–2 weeks at room temperature with the stems in water, or 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.

You can, but no timeline is given because freeze damage will appear — the needles darken and soften. The flavour holds up, so frozen sprigs are fine in a braise; drying is the better option otherwise.

faq.q: Does rosemary need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Not immediately. It will do 1–2 weeks in water on the counter, but the fridge roughly doubles that.

zh.name: 新鮮迷迭香
zh.summary: 新鮮迷迭香把莖插在水裡放室溫可放 1～2 週，放 4 °C 以下冷藏則是 2～3 週。它的針葉硬挺、帶蠟質又富樹脂，這就是它比蔬果室裡任何一種軟莖香草都耐放的原因。
zh.pantry: 插在裝了一點水的瓶子裡、避免直曬、每天換水，可放 1～2 週。迷迭香是地中海灌木，乾燥空氣正合它的胃口；它在檯面上的結局是慢慢變乾，而不是腐爛，而乾燥迷迭香本來就是好用的食材。木質的莖泡水太久，切口會開始發黏，所以換水時順手把切口剪掉一小截。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 2～3 週：用乾的廚房紙巾鬆鬆包起來，裝袋或裝盒放蔬果室。要下鍋時才洗——針葉排水很差，卡在莖邊的水就一直留在那裡。袋子不要貼著冰箱內壁，那裡會把針葉凍黑。放幾天後若紙巾摸起來潮濕，就換一張乾的。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給冷凍期限，因為冷凍一定會出現凍傷：針葉會變深、變軟，解凍後的枝條也沒辦法乾淨地把葉子剝下來。不過它的風味很耐凍，因為味道大半在樹脂類精油裡，而不是脆弱的揮發性成分裡，所以冷凍的枝條直接丟進燉鍋或烤盤還是好用。如果這道菜看得到、咬得到香草本身，那就把多的拿去陰乾——整束倒掛在通風處，乾了再把針葉剝進罐子。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍。冷凍的枝條直接丟進鍋裡、湯裡或烤盤裡。
spoilage: 針葉變黑或變深褐，而不是原本的灰綠色。
泡過水的木質莖切口發黏。
密封袋裡的莖上長出白色或灰色絨毛。
捏碎一根針葉完全聞不到樹脂香。
tips: 剝針葉要逆著生長方向往下擼；順著只會把葉子撕爛。
剝完的光莖別丟，拿來當烤肉籤很好用。
多出來的拿去陰乾，別冷凍；迷迭香大概是最耐乾燥的香草。
早一點下鍋，不要最後才放：樹脂類精油需要熱和時間才出得來。

faq.q: 新鮮迷迭香可以放多久？
faq.a: 莖插水放室溫 1～2 週，或 4 °C 以下冷藏 2～3 週。

faq.q: 新鮮迷迭香可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 可以，但沒有給期限，因為一定會凍傷——針葉會變深變軟。風味倒是留得住，所以冷凍枝條拿去燉煮沒問題；其他情況陰乾更好。
不用馬上冰。插水放檯面撐得過 1～2 週，但冰箱大約可以讓它多放一倍的時間。
